# Introduction

This report analyzes the processed time-course data from Step 2. Its primary goal is to calculate growth rates over different time periods (defined in the YAML configuration file for this run, named in the table below) and visualize how different treatments affect cell growth over time.

This analysis helps identify if a drug has an early (cytostatic) vs. late (cytotoxic) effect, or if its effect is constant across the experiment.

# Key Output Files

This report generates both data tables and plots:

* **`tables/grow_rates.csv`:** A long-format table with the calculated growth rate (`rate`, `sd_rate`) for every treatment, cell line, and time period (`range`). It also includes the normalized `plot_value` used for the bar plots.
* **`tables/grow_rates_wide.csv`:** The same growth rate data, but pivoted to a wide format where columns are cell lines.
* **`plots/cell_count_curves_...pdf`:** A multi-page PDF document containing the final time-series and growth-rate bar plots for each cell line and treatment comparison, as defined in the config file.

# Data transformation

```{r packages}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

```

## Read Plotting Configurations

All parameters for this analysis report are controlled by the YAML configuration file staged in the `raw_data` folder. The exact file used by *this* run, and whether it came from you or was generated in Step 1, are the first two rows of the table below.

This file defines the time periods, normalization strategy, and plots to be generated. Below is a description of each key parameter, using the file from this run as an example.

```{r read_config}
wd <- "{{output_dir}}"
config_arg <- "{{{configuration_file_path}}}"
config_path <- resolve_incucyte_config_path(config_arg, wd)
config <- read_yaml(config_path)

# Create a summary table of key config parameters
config_summary <- data.table(
  Parameter = character(),
  Description = character(),
  Value = character()
)

# Prepare display values for x-axis settings
# Default theme_bw() axis text size is approx 9pt (base_size 11 * 0.8)
x_axis_show_val <- if (is.null(config$x_axis_text_show)) TRUE else as.logical(config$x_axis_text_show)
x_axis_size_str <- if (is.null(config$x_axis_text_size)) "9 (Default)" else as.character(config$x_axis_text_size)

# Which file these numbers came from. A run started without a configuration is analysed with
# windows derived from the data, which is a very different claim from the one a reader makes when
# they supplied their own - so both the file and its origin are stated here rather than assumed.
if (nzchar(config_arg)) {
  config_source <- "supplied with the run"
} else {
  config_source <- "generated in Step 1 from the data (defaults)"
}

# Add basic parameters
config_summary <- rbindlist(list(
  config_summary,
  data.table(
    Parameter = "config_file",
    Description = "Configuration file this report read",
    Value = sub(paste0("^", wd, "/"), "", config_path)
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "config_source",
    Description = "Where that file came from",
    Value = config_source
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "plot_date",
    Description = "Date string for output file naming",
    Value = as.character(config$plot_date)
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "cell_lines",
    Description = "Cell line(s) to analyze and plot",
    Value = paste(config$cell_lines, collapse = ", ")
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "early_period",
    Description = "Time window (hours) for early growth rate calculation",
    Value = paste(config$early_period, collapse = " - ")
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "late_period",
    Description = "Time window (hours) for late growth rate calculation",
    Value = paste(config$late_period, collapse = " - ")
  )
))

# Add mid_period if defined
if (!is.null(config$mid_period)) {
  config_summary <- rbindlist(list(
    config_summary,
    data.table(
      Parameter = "mid_period",
      Description = "Time window (hours) for mid growth rate calculation (optional)",
      Value = paste(config$mid_period, collapse = " - ")
    )
  ))
}

# Add normalization and scaling parameters
config_summary <- rbindlist(list(
  config_summary,
  data.table(
    Parameter = "y_axis_scaling",
    Description = "Y-axis scaling strategy for bar plots",
    Value = as.character(config$y_axis_scaling)
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "x_axis_text_show",
    Description = "Show x-axis text on bar plots (TRUE/FALSE)",
    Value = as.character(x_axis_show_val)
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "x_axis_text_size",
    Description = "Font size for x-axis text (if shown)",
    Value = x_axis_size_str
  ),
  data.table(
    Parameter = "normalization_map",
    Description = "Normalization targets for each period",
    Value = paste(names(config$normalization_map), "→", unlist(config$normalization_map), collapse = "; ")
  )
))

generate_datatable(config_summary, options = list(pageLength = 20))

```

### Config File Breakdown

The table above shows the key parameters from your configuration file. Below is additional detail on the most important settings:

* **`normalization_map`**: Controls normalization for bar plots. For each period (`early`, `mid`, `late`), you specify a `norm_target`:
* **`"None"`**: Use the raw log2 growth rate.
* **`"early"`**: Normalize by the **'early' DMSO** growth rate (relative value where 1.0 = DMSO control).


* **`treatment_comparisons`**: Defines which treatments to plot side-by-side (one page per comparison in the output PDF).

## Reading Data

This section loads the processed data from Step 2 (`gDR_mae.qs2`). This object contains the `LogFoldChange` assay, which has been normalized relative to time 0 (log2 scale).

```{r read_in_data}
mae <- qs_read(file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_mae.qs2"))

# Extract the time-course experiment
se <- mae[[get_supported_experiments("time-course")]]

# Extract the normalized data directly into a data.table.
# convert_se_assay_to_dt automatically merges rowData and colData.
# The assay name comes from the time-course fit profile rather than a literal,
# so the report reads whatever gDRcore fits on even if that default changes.
lfc_assay <- gDRutils::get_fit_profile("time-course")$input_assay
all_data <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(se, lfc_assay)

# Ensure it is a data.table
setDT(all_data)


```

This helper function creates a clean treatment label for plotting (e.g., "DrugA 10uM + DrugB 5uM").

```{r add_treatment_names}
all_data <- add_treatment_column(dt = all_data)

```

# Calculating Time-Specific Growth Rates

To understand the dynamics of the drug response, we don't just look at the endpoint. This section calculates the log2 growth rate (via a linear model) for distinct time periods (e.g., `early`, `mid`, `late`) defined in the config.

## Defining events

Defining the periods from the config file to be used for calculation and plotting.

```{r defining_events}

# Start with the baseline 'treatment' event
events <- data.table(
  name = c("treatment"),
  Duration = c(10))

# Dynamically add periods from config
period_names <- c()
period_durations <- c()

if (!is.null(config$early_period)) {
  period_names <- c(period_names, "early")
  # ensure period durations are numeric (handles potential config parsing issues)
  period_durations <- c(period_durations, mean(as.numeric(config$early_period)))
}
if (!is.null(config$mid_period)) {
  period_names <- c(period_names, "mid")
  period_durations <- c(period_durations, mean(as.numeric(config$mid_period)))
}
if (!is.null(config$late_period)) {
  period_names <- c(period_names, "late")
  period_durations <- c(period_durations, mean(as.numeric(config$late_period)))
}

# Bind the new periods to the events data.frame
if (length(period_names) > 0) {
  events <- rbindlist(list(events,
                 data.table(name = period_names, Duration = period_durations)))
}

```

## Data combinations

This table shows all unique combinations of Cell Line, Treatment, and Plate Barcode found in the data.

```{r data_combinations}
trt_list <- unique(all_data[, .(treatment)])
u_combs <- unique(all_data[, .(CellLineName, treatment, Barcode)])
generate_datatable(u_combs, options = list(pageLength = 15))

```

# Computing Growth Rates Per Time Period (Long format)

In this section the growth rate is calculated for each period, then aggregated, and normalized, based on the normalization_map in the config.

For example, the growth rate of the `mid` and `late` periods can be normalized to the growth rate of the `early` DMSO control. This creates a relative growth rate, allowing you to see how the change in growth rate compares to the control.

The first table below lists the measurement timepoints that each window contains. Read it before the rates: a window is defined by bounds, but the fit only ever sees the measurements that fall inside them, and a window placed close to the sampling grid can hold fewer points than intended. Note the listing is the union across all plates in the dataset, so on a uniform sampling grid it describes every well, but if plates were read on different schedules it is an upper bound rather than a per-well count.

```{r calc_growth_rates}

# Create a list of periods to process from the config
periods_to_process <- list()
if (is.null(config$early_period)) {
  stop("Error: 'early_period' must be defined in config.")
} else {
  periods_to_process$early <- config$early_period
}

if (!is.null(config$mid_period)) periods_to_process$mid <- config$mid_period
if (!is.null(config$late_period)) periods_to_process$late <- config$late_period

# Check for normalization_map
if (is.null(config$normalization_map)) {
  stop("Error: 'normalization_map' block missing from YAML config file.")
}
if (!all(names(periods_to_process) %in% names(config$normalization_map))) {
  stop("Error: 'normalization_map' is missing an entry for one or more defined periods (e.g., early, mid, late).")
}


# Growth rates are computed by compute_growth_rates() from gDRcore, the stage 1
# of fit_SE.timecourse(). The report used to carry its own copy of this logic; a
# single implementation keeps the report and the package from drifting apart.
# Note the time windows are half-open [start, end): a timepoint on the boundary
# between two contiguous periods belongs to the later one, and t = 0 is kept.
periods_num <- lapply(periods_to_process, as.numeric)
norm_map <- unlist(config$normalization_map)[names(periods_to_process)]

# State which measurements each window actually contains. The bounds on their
# own are ambiguous - whether a timepoint sitting exactly on a boundary counts
# depends on the window convention - and a window can silently hold far fewer
# points than intended. gDRcore answers this with the same rule it fits on.
period_timepoints <- gDRcore::get_period_timepoints(se, periods_num)
generate_datatable(period_timepoints)

growth_dt <- gDRcore::compute_growth_rates(
  se,
  periods = periods_num,
  normalization_map = norm_map
)

# Attach the report treatment label by joining on the drug/concentration
# identifiers, so the labels match the rest of the report exactly.
id_keys <- c("drug_name", "drug_name2", "drug_name3",
             "concentration", "concentration2", "concentration3")
id_cols <- unlist(get_env_identifiers(id_keys, simplify = FALSE))
join_cols <- intersect(id_cols, intersect(names(all_data), names(growth_dt)))
if (length(join_cols) == 0) {
  # merge(by = character(0)) silently degrades to a cartesian join
  stop("Error: no shared drug/concentration identifier to join the treatment labels on.")
}
trt_map <- unique(all_data[, c(join_cols, "treatment"), with = FALSE])
growth_dt <- merge(growth_dt, trt_map, by = join_cols, all.x = TRUE)

if (anyNA(growth_dt$treatment)) {
  stop("Error: could not resolve a treatment label for every growth rate row.")
}

# rate_0 is guaranteed by compute_growth_rates() on every path, controls or not.
setnames(growth_dt,
         c("period", "GrowthRate", "sd_GrowthRate"),
         c("range", "rate", "sd_rate"))

# One row per (cell line, treatment, period). Several drug/concentration
# groups collapsing into one label would be a labelling problem, not a data
# problem, so warn rather than fail.
key_cols <- c("CellLineName", "treatment", "range")
if (anyDuplicated(growth_dt, by = key_cols) > 0) {
  warning("Several drug/concentration groups share a treatment label; averaging them.")
  growth_dt <- growth_dt[, .(rate = mean(rate, na.rm = TRUE),
                             sd_rate = mean(sd_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
                             rate_0 = mean(rate_0, na.rm = TRUE),
                             NormalizedGrowthRate = mean(NormalizedGrowthRate, na.rm = TRUE)),
                         by = key_cols]
}

# --- PER-PHASE NORMALIZATION ---
# compute_growth_rates() already applied normalization_map: NormalizedGrowthRate
# is the raw rate for "None" periods and rate / control rate otherwise, with
# rate_0 holding the control baseline that was used.
norm_df <- data.table(range = names(norm_map), norm_target = unname(norm_map))

cat("\n--- Applying Normalization Map ---\n")
print(norm_df)

av_rates <- merge(growth_dt[, c(key_cols, "rate", "sd_rate", "rate_0",
                                "NormalizedGrowthRate"), with = FALSE],
                  norm_df, by = "range")

av_rates[, is_normalized := norm_target != "None"]
av_rates[, rel_rates := ifelse(is_normalized, NormalizedGrowthRate, NA_real_)]
av_rates[, rel_rates_sd := ifelse(is_normalized, sd_rate / abs(rate_0), NA_real_)]
av_rates[, plot_value := ifelse(is_normalized, rel_rates, rate)]
av_rates[, plot_sd := ifelse(is_normalized, rel_rates_sd, sd_rate)]
av_rates[, rate_0 := ifelse(is_normalized, rate_0, NA_real_)]
av_rates[, NormalizedGrowthRate := NULL]

cat("--- Control Baseline Rates (for normalization lookup) ---\n")
print(unique(av_rates[is_normalized == TRUE, .(CellLineName, norm_target, rate_0)]))

# Restore the plotting order of periods and treatments
av_rates[, range := factor(range, levels = names(periods_to_process))]
av_rates[, treatment := factor(treatment, levels = trt_list$treatment)]
setcolorder(av_rates, c("range", "CellLineName", "treatment", "rate",
                        "sd_rate", "norm_target", "rate_0", "rel_rates",
                        "rel_rates_sd", "plot_value", "plot_sd",
                        "is_normalized"))


# This handles the edge-case  for the "all None" normalization case.
# Identify all potential numeric columns
potential_num_cols <- c("rate", "sd_rate", "plot_value", "plot_sd", "rel_rates", "rel_rates_sd", "rate_0")

# Find which of these columns actually exist in av_rates
existing_num_cols <- intersect(potential_num_cols, colnames(av_rates))

# Check which of these existing columns are NOT all NA
if (length(existing_num_cols) > 0) {
  are_not_all_na <- sapply(av_rates[, ..existing_num_cols], function(col) !all(is.na(col)))
  # The columns to round are the ones that exist and are not all NA
  round_cols <- existing_num_cols[are_not_all_na]
} else {
  round_cols <- c() # No numeric columns found to round
}

generate_datatable(av_rates, col_to_round = round_cols, options = list(pageLength = 15))
gr_fpath <- file.path(wd, "tables", "grow_rates.csv")
fwrite(av_rates, gr_fpath)

```

**What to look for in the table: Scan the `av_rates` table above.**

* Check the `plot_value` column. For 'Raw' phases (`is_normalized: FALSE`), this is the raw log2 growth rate.
* For normalized phases (`is_normalized: TRUE`), a value of 1.0 means the growth rate is identical to the control (e.g., 'early' DMSO). A value < 1.0 indicates growth inhibition, and < 0 indicates cell death.

## Wide format

This is the same data as above, but pivoted to a wide format where cell lines are columns, which may be more convenient for some users.

```{r grow_rates_wide_format}

av_wide_rates <- cast_to_wide(
  long_data = av_rates,
  id_vars   = c("treatment", "range"),
  col_var   = "CellLineName",
  val_var   = "rate"
)

# Ensure av_wide_rates is explicitly a data.table to satisfy check_class assertions
setDT(av_wide_rates)

round_cols2 <- colnames(av_wide_rates)[!colnames(av_wide_rates) %in% c("CellLineName", "treatment", "range")]
generate_datatable(av_wide_rates, col_to_round = round_cols2, options = list(pageLength = 15))
gr_wide_fpath <- file.path(wd, "tables", "grow_rates_wide.csv")
fwrite(av_wide_rates, gr_wide_fpath)


```

## Combined treatment names

This section aggregates the data by treatment and time point for visualization. The `LogFoldChange` (`CellCount_norm`) is used directly from the processed assay.

```{r aggregate_treatments}
# Use data.table aggregation instead of aggregate()
# LogFoldChange is already the normalized value we want (log2 fold change from T0)
df_av <- all_data[, .(CellCount_norm = mean(LogFoldChange, na.rm = TRUE),
                      sd_CellCount = sd(LogFoldChange, na.rm = TRUE)),
                  by = .(Duration, CellLineName, treatment)]

ct <- data.table(combined_treaments = sort(levels(unique(av_rates$treatment))))
generate_datatable(ct, options = list(pageLength = 15))

```

In this section a SummarizedExperiment object is created, to hold the normalized data for plotting.

```{r create_se}

filtered_df_av <- df_av[CellLineName %in% config$cell_line, ]

# Vectorized pivot: Duration x treatment matrices via dcast
summarized_experiment_normalized <- as.matrix(
  data.table::dcast(filtered_df_av, Duration ~ treatment, value.var = "CellCount_norm"),
  rownames = "Duration"
)
# Raw counts placeholder (plot only uses NormalizedCellCounts)
summarized_experiment_raw_counts <- matrix(1,
  nrow = NROW(summarized_experiment_normalized),
  ncol = ncol(summarized_experiment_normalized),
  dimnames = dimnames(summarized_experiment_normalized)
)

se <- SummarizedExperiment(
  assays = list(CellCounts = summarized_experiment_raw_counts,
                NormalizedCellCounts = summarized_experiment_normalized),
  rowData = rownames(summarized_experiment_normalized),
  colData = colnames(summarized_experiment_normalized))

metadata(se)$CellLineName <- config$cell_line

```

# Plot Cell Count Fold-Change

The following plots visualize the results for each cell line defined in the config file. Each plot is a 2-panel figure:

**What to look for (Top: Line Plot):**

* This plot shows the log2(Cell count fold-change) over time (relative to T=0).
* **Control (DMSO):** This is your baseline for normal growth.
* **Treatment Curves:** Observe how the colored treatment lines diverge from the control. Do they flatten out (cytostatic) or go down (cytotoxic)?
* **Shaded Regions:** These correspond to the `early`, `mid`, and `late` periods where growth rates are calculated.

**What to look for (Bottom: Bar Plot):**

* This plot summarizes the calculated growth rate from the line plot for each period.
* **Raw Rate (e.g., `early` phase):** The y-axis is the raw log2 growth rate.
* **Normalized Rate (e.g., `mid`, `late` phases):** The y-axis is the relative growth rate. The gray line at y=1 represents the control growth rate (from the `early` phase). Bars significantly below 1 show strong growth inhibition in that specific period.

```{r process_and_plot_cell_lines, results='asis', comment=NA}

# In this section all cell lines specified in the config are analyzed, 
# a SummarizedExperiment object is generated, as well as plots, and embedded PDFs.

# --- 1. Get Cell Lines ---
# Ensure config$cell_lines is defined. 
# If not, try to fall back to old config$cell_line for robustness.
if (is.null(config$cell_lines)) {
  if (!is.null(config$cell_line)) {
    config$cell_lines <- c(config$cell_line)
    warning("Config parameter 'cell_lines' not found. Falling back to 'cell_line'.")
  } else {
    stop("No 'cell_lines' or 'cell_line' found in config file.")
  }
}

# --- 2. Start Loop ---
for (current_cell_line in config$cell_lines) {
  
  # Print markdown header for this cell line section
  cat(paste("\n\n---\n\n# 🔬 Plots for Cell Line:", current_cell_line, "\n\n"))
  
  # --- 3. Opening Output Directory (Moved from above) ---
  dir.create(file.path(wd, "plots"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  # use current_cell_line in the file name
  # snitize cell line name for the file path
  # this removes special characters like '#' and '()' which can break embedding
  safe_cell_line_name <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_ -]", "", current_cell_line)
  
  # Build the filename using the "safe" name
  pdf_filename <- paste0("cell_count_curves_", config$plot_date, "_", safe_cell_line_name, ".pdf")
  
  # Replace spaces with underscores
  pdf_filename <- gsub(' ', '_', pdf_filename) 
  
  # Set the final paths
  rel_output_pdf_path <- file.path("plots", pdf_filename)
  output_pdf_path <- file.path(wd, rel_output_pdf_path)
  
  # --- 4. Create SummarizedExperiment
  
  # filter df_av for the current cell line in the loop
  filtered_df_av <- df_av[CellLineName == current_cell_line]
  
  # Check if data exists for this cell line
  if (nrow(filtered_df_av) == 0) {
    cat(paste0("<p style='color:red;'><strong>Warning:</strong> No data found for cell line: ", 
               current_cell_line, ". Skipping plots for this cell line.</p>"))
    next # Skip to the next iteration of the loop
  }
  
  # Vectorized pivot: Duration x treatment matrices via dcast
  summarized_experiment_normalized <- as.matrix(
    data.table::dcast(filtered_df_av, Duration ~ treatment, value.var = "CellCount_norm"),
    rownames = "Duration"
  )
  # Raw counts placeholder — df_av holds only LogFoldChange (CellCount_norm);
  # raw cell counts are not available at this stage so we use a ones matrix.
  summarized_experiment_raw_counts <- matrix(1L,
    nrow = nrow(summarized_experiment_normalized),
    ncol = ncol(summarized_experiment_normalized),
    dimnames = dimnames(summarized_experiment_normalized)
  )

  se <- SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(CellCounts = summarized_experiment_raw_counts,
                  NormalizedCellCounts = summarized_experiment_normalized),
    rowData = rownames(summarized_experiment_normalized),
    colData = colnames(summarized_experiment_normalized))
  
  # set metadata to the current cell line
  metadata(se)$CellLineName <- current_cell_line
  

  # --- 5. Plot Cell Count Fold-Change (Moved from above) ---
  
  pdf(output_pdf_path, 8, 6)
   
  for (sel_trt in config$treatment_comparisons) {
    trt_names <- sel_trt
    trt_names <- gsub(' \\+', '\n+', trt_names)
      
    trt_colors <- config$all_colors[1:length(sel_trt)]
    names(trt_colors) <- trt_names
    
    # This function is now generic and will use the 'se' metadata
    sel_av <- filter_treatments(se, sel_trt) 
    sel_av$Duration <- as.numeric(sel_av$Duration)
    sel_av$treatment <- factor(sel_av$treatment, sel_trt)
    levels(sel_av$treatment) <- trt_names
    
    # filter sel_rates by the current_cell_line as well
    # The 'range' column here is now a factor with the correct levels
    sel_rates <- av_rates[treatment %in% sel_trt & CellLineName == current_cell_line] 
    
    sel_rates$treatment <- factor(sel_rates$treatment, sel_trt)
    levels(sel_rates$treatment) <- trt_names
    y_max <- max(sel_av$CellCount_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # calculate negative y-limit so cytotoxic curves aren't cut off at 0
    y_min <- min(sel_av$CellCount_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
    y_min_limit <- min(0, y_min)
    
    x_max <- max(all_data$Duration, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # --- DYNAMIC PLOTTING ---
    
    # 1. Build the base line plot
    p1 <- ggplot(sel_av, aes(x = Duration, color = treatment, y = CellCount_norm))
    
    # 2. Create a data.table for period rectangles
    period_df <- data.table(
      name = character(),
      xmin = numeric(),
      xmax = numeric(),
      fill = character()
    )
    if (!is.null(config$early_period)) {
      period_df <- rbindlist(list(period_df, data.table(name = "early", xmin = config$early_period[1], xmax = config$early_period[2], fill = "#ffffdd")))
    }
    if (!is.null(config$mid_period)) {
      # Add a new color for the mid period
      period_df <- rbindlist(list(period_df, data.table(name = "mid", xmin = config$mid_period[1], xmax = config$mid_period[2], fill = "#ddffff"))) # light cyan
    }
    if (!is.null(config$late_period)) {
      period_df <- rbindlist(list(period_df, data.table(name = "late", xmin = config$late_period[1], xmax = config$late_period[2], fill = "#ffddff")))
    }
    
    # 3. Add dynamic layers
    if (NROW(period_df) > 0) {
      p1 <- p1 + geom_rect(data = period_df, 
                          aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = name), 
                          alpha = 0.8, color = 'white', inherit.aes = FALSE) +
                  # Use scale_fill_manual to assign the correct colors
                  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(period_df$fill, period_df$name), guide = "none")
    }
    
    # Add vlines and text (which use the dynamic 'events' data.table)
    p1 <- p1 +
      geom_vline(xintercept = events$Duration) + # Dynamically plots all vlines
      geom_text(data = events, 
                aes(y = y_max + .1, label = name, x = Duration), # Explicitly set aes
                color = 'black', angle = 90, vjust = 1, hjust = 1, 
                inherit.aes = FALSE) + # Disable aes inheritance
      scale_color_manual(values = trt_colors)+
      # use dynamic y_min_limit
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_min_limit, y_max+.3), xlim = c(0, 1.001 * x_max))+
      geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
      ylab('log2(Cell count fold-change)')+
      xlab('Time (h)')+
      ggtitle(metadata(se)$CellLineName) +
      theme_bw()
    
    # 4. Build the bar plot (p2)
    
    # --- Set Y-Axis Scaling ---
    if (is.null(config$y_axis_scaling)) {
      y_axis_scales <- "free_y" 
    } else {
      y_axis_scales <- config$y_axis_scaling
    }
    if (!y_axis_scales %in% c("free_y", "fixed")) {
      warning(paste("Invalid 'y_axis_scaling' value:", y_axis_scales, ". Defaulting to 'free_y'."))
      y_axis_scales <- "free_y"
    }
    
    # 1. Create the base plot
    p2 <- ggplot(sel_rates, 
                 aes(x = treatment, fill = treatment, y = plot_value)) +
        
        # This hline at 0 is always present
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = 'gray') +
        
        geom_col(linewidth = 1, width = .6, position = 'dodge') + 
        
        # Error bars now use the generic 'plot_sd'
        geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(ymin = plot_value - plot_sd, 
                                    ymax = plot_value + plot_sd), 
                      width = .3) +
        
        theme(legend.position = "none") +
        theme_bw() +
        scale_colour_grey(guide = "none") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = trt_colors)
        
    # --- X-Axis Text Logic ---
    # Default to TRUE if not specified in config
    show_x_text <- if (is.null(config$x_axis_text_show)) TRUE else as.logical(config$x_axis_text_show)
    
    # Use specified size or default (9) if NULL
    x_text_size <- if (is.null(config$x_axis_text_size)) 9 else as.numeric(config$x_axis_text_size)
    
    if (show_x_text) {
       p2 <- p2 + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = x_text_size))
    } else {
      p2 <- p2 + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
    }
    
    p2 <- p2 + 
        # The 'scales' argument is controlled by the config variable
        facet_wrap(vars(range), scales = y_axis_scales) +
        
        # A generic y-axis label, as units may be mixed
        ylab("Value (Normalized or Raw Rate)")
        

    # 2. Conditionally add the y=1 hline
    # This check prevents the "all None" scaling bug.
    if (any(sel_rates$is_normalized == TRUE)) {
      p2 <- p2 + 
        # This hline at 1 is only drawn for facets where 'is_normalized' is TRUE
        # uses a subsetting function on the data passed to the plot
        geom_hline(data = function(x) x[is_normalized == TRUE], 
               yintercept = 1, color = 'gray')
    }
        
    # 5. Arrange the plots
    print(patchwork::wrap_plots(p1, p2, ncol = 1))
  }
  invisible(dev.off())
  
  
  # --- 6. Embed PDF
  # This prints the embed tag to the markdown output
  cat(paste0('\n\n<embed src="', rel_output_pdf_path, '" width="100%" height="600px" type="application/pdf">\n\n'))
  
} # --- End of for loop ---
```
